notes.note: Genesis 8:1 is retained as a narrative water/wind parallel. It is not a claim that the source words for wind and Spirit have been independently collated or that the two scenes are identical.
John 1:4-5 is a theological light/darkness analogy. It is not labelled a quotation of this individual verse.
Same-chapter evening/morning refrains are literary cross-references. Each source/target direction is a distinct pair; no inference of historical dependence between adjacent verses is intended.
Firmament and upper-water language is retained from the supplied edition without a new cosmological or scientific interpretation.
Genesis 8:17 repeats multiplication language at the creatures' release, while the command in the supplied English reading addresses Noah.

Connections with Sirach, Wisdom, Psalms and James concern image, human dignity and responsibility toward creatures. No independent original-language collation or specialist doctrinal adjudication is claimed.
The supplied Greek-based Genesis 2:2 says God completed His work on the sixth day. That source wording is preserved; it is not silently replaced by a different edition's seventh-day reading.
The supplied Genesis says completion on the sixth day and rest on the seventh. Hebrews quotes the rest clause. The supplied sixth-day completion reading remains intact.

The supplied Job says divine spirit made the speaker and the Almighty's breath teaches him. The retained comparison concerns divine agency and clay; it does not replace the teaching statement with another edition's life-giving-breath wording. This distinction was corrected during peer QA.
The named-river comparison uses actual Sirach units 25-27, with no missing 24:24 unit inserted. No modern location or reconstruction of Eden's river courses is asserted.

Later marriage and formation texts are linked to the actual creation passages. The comparison does not claim that all later statements on authority, childbearing, Christ or the Church occur explicitly in Genesis.
The woman says nor shall you touch it in this supplied text. The earlier command at Genesis 2:17 is quoted exactly; no new conclusion about an omitted divine command or textual error is imposed.

The supplied Greek-based wording is He shall watch for your head, and you shall watch for his heel. Romans 16:20 and Luke 10:19 are labelled later Christian thematic associations, not quotations or a claim that Genesis itself uses the word crush or explicitly names Satan.
The link records shared references to Eve, transgression and childbearing. It does not settle the interpretation of saved through childbearing or adjudicate gender roles.
The source names the woman Life in Genesis 3:20 and Eve in Genesis 4:1. Both labels are retained rather than silently standardized.
No claim is made that the skin garments establish a sacrifice, blood atonement or a particular typology; the retained links concern actual clothing and divine provision.

The supplied text concerns offering rightly and dividing rightly, then says Be still. His turning shall be toward you, and you shall rule over him. Familiar sin crouching wording is not imported. The final pronoun reference and the full ritual interpretation remain unadjudicated; retained parallels concern worship and conduct only.

The supplied edition reads My guilt is too great for me to be forgiven. Cross-references contrast that wording with forgiveness texts; they do not replace it with an alternate punishment-too-great reading or infer a settled psychological diagnosis.

The Cain-line Enoch, Methuselah and Lamech must not be merged with names in Seth's line. Genesis 4:18 retains Gaidad, Maiel and Methuselah exactly as supplied. Genealogical cross-references are labelled contrasts, not identical-person matches.
Comparison with the one-flesh text identifies a narrative difference between Lamech's two wives and the earlier pair. It does not invent an explicit divine judgment at Genesis 4:19.

The Exodus range is limited to corresponding bodily injuries. Its surrounding Greek-based fetal-formation case at Exodus 21:22-23 was read; this review does not restate it as an unrelated universal legal rule or adjudicate its disputed implications.
The source reads He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God. The record does not replace this with a different edition's statement about people first beginning worship.

Chronological correspondence pairs check only the arithmetic of the supplied Genesis ages. They do not harmonize those ages with another biblical edition or claim that Chronicles or Luke supplies matching ages.

Chronicles names Kenan where the supplied Genesis and Luke records use Cainan. The retained link is their corresponding position between Enosh and Mahalalel in the ancestry, with the English-name difference stated explicitly.

The supplied Enoch chronology is 165 years before Methuselah plus 200 afterward, totaling 365. Preserve that reading. Wisdom 4:10-14 does not name Enoch and is retained only as an approval-and-transfer thematic parallel.

The supplied Methuselah figures are 167 plus 802, totaling 969; Lamech is 188 plus 565, totaling 753. These exact source readings are not silently replaced by figures from another edition. This Seth-line Lamech is not equated with Cain-line Lamech in Genesis 4.
Marriage and offspring links retain the source language without resolving the disputed identity of the sons of God. No proposed angelic, Sethite or royal identification is counted as established.
The hundred and twenty years remain uninterpreted as to lifespan limit versus a period before judgment. The Peter patience link does not decide that question.
The supplied English says God took to heart and pondered. The rationale does not substitute the wording repented or regretted from a different textual stream.
Hebrews recalls ark preparation but does not repeat its measurements or roof specification. Those limits are stated in the relevant rationales; the tapering roof is not silently called a window.

The general pair instructions and later clean-creature sevens remain distinct. The retained fulfilment links quote the actual entrance passages rather than claiming that every later animal detail says only two.

The comprehensive obedience formula is a literary parallel in divine construction instructions. The two structures are not identified. The supplied Exodus context has no separate 40:7 or 40:11 units; neither missing unit is used as a target.

The supplied edition dates the opening flood, ark rest and final drying on the twenty-seventh day, rather than silently importing other editions' seventeenth-day readings. No reconstructed day-count calendar is asserted.

The supplied text says waters diminished until the tenth month and mountain tops appeared in the eleventh month. Both statements are preserved; no harmonization or independent textual-critical resolution is claimed.
The Genesis 1:2 comparison concerns divine action over waters before habitable ground appears. It does not identify wind and Spirit as identical or claim new original-language verification.
Clean-creature and burnt-offering comparisons with Leviticus are labelled thematic. They do not claim Noah had been given the later Sinai legislation.
The source's multiplication command is addressed to Noah at the release of creatures. It is not rewritten as an unambiguous command spoken directly to the animals.
The Acts food/blood comparison cites the actual apostolic letter at Acts 15:28-29 after reading the decision context, rather than attributing James' earlier proposal to a completed letter.
Actual target reading corrected the candidate numbering: in this Greek-based Exodus, 20:13 prohibits adultery, 20:14 theft, and 20:15 murder. The retained murder comparison uses 20:15.

Noah's creature-wide covenant, Abraham's covenant and Israel's Sabbath sign are compared as covenant forms; their audiences and provisions are not conflated. Ezekiel's rainbow is a shared image, not a restatement of Noah's covenant.

The review adds no unreported sexual act to Ham's behavior. The curse names Canaan; it is not transferred to all Ham's descendants or racial groups. Joshua 9:23 is a limited curse-and-servitude parallel.
The supplied pronoun in the dwelling clause is retained. The comparisons do not resolve whether its subject is God or Japheth.
Retain Elishah in both supplied Japheth/Javan lists and Cainan in both supplied Shem and Arphaxad contexts. Cross-references do not remove or harmonize these differing placements.

The available Chronicles text contains no separate 1:11-16 or 1:18-23 units. Only actual available units are used. English forms such as Kitians/Kittians, Regma/Raamah, Sala/Shelah and Ragau/Reu remain distinct in their quoted sources.

Nimrod remains a giant hunter before the Lord in the supplied text. No claim that before means rebellion, or that Nimrod built the later tower, is added. Dasem is retained and the great-city clause is not independently resolved.
The nations comparison retains Deuteronomy's angels-of-God wording without forcing a traditional number of peoples or mapping the genealogies onto modern racial identities.
Language settings and comprehension are compared thematically. Acts is not described as explicitly quoting Babel or declaring a reversal of Genesis 11:1.

The descent-and-seeing parallel preserves the supplied Sodom wording about being brought to an end according to the cry; a familiar alternate formulation about what the people have done was removed during peer QA.

Luke and Chronicles links establish corresponding genealogical positions only. They do not corroborate Genesis's ages, unnamed children or death notices. The combined Arphaxad/Cainan material remains within the original 11:13 anchor.

Do not merge the ancestor Nahor with Terah's son of the same name, Haran the deceased man with Harran the destination, or Iscah with Sara. Sara is the supplied name here and changes to Sarah at17:15. Acts7 and Nehemiah9 supply retrospective divine-action perspectives; no forced reconstruction of Terah's or Abram's birth years is imposed.

Acts places the initial appearance before residence at Haran and narrates movement after the father's death. The records preserve its presentation alongside Genesis rather than imposing a new chronological harmonization.

The supplied Genesis says all the tribes of the earth in Abram; later texts speak of nations or families and, in Acts, the seed. These are labelled explicit reuse and interpretation without replacing the supplied English wording.
The connections concern Shechem and patriarchal acts there. The oak and the later terebinth are not asserted to be the same individual tree or parcel.
The supplied text says wilderness. No alternate Negev wording, precise geographical reconstruction or modern travel itinerary is inserted.

The later wife-and-sister episodes in Genesis 20 and 26 are narrative parallels. The comparison does not identify their rulers as one historical person, approve the deception, or claim identical circumstances. Sara and Sarah labels remain as supplied.
The family term brother is read alongside Genesis 12:5, which explicitly identifies Lot as Abram's brother's son. No biological brother relationship is substituted.
The supplied Genesis uses sand of the earth. Sirach 44:21 uses dust and stars; the related multitude imagery is retained with its own wording rather than made an exact verbal quotation.

The supplied king names, nations, giants, Ommaeans, rulers of Amalek, Salt Sea and itinerary remain intact. No modern identification of kings, reconstructed campaign route or resolution of possible chronological/geographical questions is claimed.

The account says the kings fled and fell into bitumen pits, and later mentions the king of Sodom meeting Abram. The retained links do not infer a death, an escape mechanism or a resolved identity question.
The supplied text repeatedly names horses. The records do not silently replace that reading with goods or a different textual stream's spoils terminology.
Man from beyond and Aunan are preserved from the supplied English. The record does not substitute Hebrew as a new lexical finding or normalize Aunan to another edition's proper name.

Melchizedek links follow the actual priesthood, blessing and tenth-giving reuse in Psalms and Hebrews. No Eucharistic interpretation is added merely from the loaves and wine, and Hebrews' theological claims are identified as that text's interpretation.
The shared household-born servant category does not establish that the later circumcision group contains exactly the same three hundred and eighteen individuals.

The supplied reading names Masek, the slave woman born in Abram's house, and Damascus Eliezer. The review does not silently substitute the familiar steward-only wording or resolve the source's household syntax.
The Hebrews link compares divine assurance of promise. The oath discussed there is not claimed to be a quotation of Genesis 15; the surrounding Hebrews quotation recalls the later Abrahamic oath.

The birds requested for the covenant scene are distinguished from birds descending on the divided bodies. The source says Abram sat down with them at 15:11; drove them away is not imported from another edition.
Not dividing the bird is a particular ritual-handling comparison. It does not equate the covenant scene with later Sinai burnt-offering legislation.

Genesis's four-hundred-year affliction prediction and Exodus's four hundred and thirty years of residence in both Egypt and Canaan remain distinct. No harmonized chronology or textual-critical resolution is asserted.

Paul explicitly interprets the two women allegorically as covenants. Links are labelled later reuse and interpretation; the Genesis narrative is not claimed to state that allegory or give a new general prescription of slavery.
The actual opposite-all-his-brothers wording is linked to Genesis 25:18. No modern ethnic or political identification is added, and wilderness residence is not equated with every conflict phrase.

The supplied well and place labels are retained: The Well Where I Saw Before Me, Well of the Vision, and Form of God. Related seeing-and-naming comparisons do not claim new Hebrew etymological or geographical verification.
The supplied divine self-identification is I am your God. The review does not replace it with Almighty or claim a newly collated divine-name reading.
Romans quotes the name explanation in 17:5. The link from 17:4 is labelled reuse and interpretation of the multinational promise, not an exact quotation of that individual verse.

The eighth-day clause in Genesis is preserved. The Exodus comparison retains its angel, circumcision statement and ambiguous pronouns; the review does not identify an unstated threatened person or replace its wording with a bridegroom-of-blood formula.

The supplied Sara-to-Sarah distinction remains. In 17:16 the later blessing pronoun is him, the promised child; it is not silently changed to her. Nehemiah's supplied Abraam spelling likewise remains in the target evidence.
Genesis reports Abraham's laughter; Romans presents his faith in the promise. Both statements are retained without substituting a psychological diagnosis or erasing either account.
The promised twelve nations are compared with the later twelvefold descendant record. Variant supplied name spellings in Genesis and Chronicles are preserved rather than normalized.
The physical covenant sign and Colossians' circumcision-not-made-by-hands interpretation remain distinguished. Genesis is not claimed to mention baptism.

God, three men and later two angels are the supplied narrative labels. No new identification of the three visitors with distinct divine persons is asserted. Hebrews 13:2 is a qualified hospitality allusion, not an explicit naming of Abraham or Lot.
Sarah's my lord refers to her husband in the supplied inward speech. The Peter link concerns that designation and does not claim a word-for-word quotation of the whole Genesis verse.

The supplied Greek-based text asks whether they are being brought to an end according to the cry. Its wording is retained; the review does not replace it with another edition's formulation or settle questions about divine knowledge.
The declining fifty-to-ten appeals are kept distinct. Jeremiah concerns Jerusalem and one person doing justice. Conditional promises are not reported as though Sodom was in fact spared.

The source reports a hostile sexual demand against guests. Jude's other flesh wording is retained as a later interpretation without resolving every phrase or making claims about modern identity groups.
The hosts' offers of women are reported actions, not divine commands or endorsements. Genesis does not say Lot's offer was carried out; the later Gibeah outcome is not imported into Sodom.

The source says sons-in-law who had taken his daughters, and later they were troubled. These are not silently rewritten as betrothed sons-in-law or Lot lingered. The review does not harmonize the daughters' status by adding unreported family members.
Wisdom's righteous fugitive, Five Cities and salt pillar are linked as particular later recollections. No new archaeological location or evidentiary claim is made.

The absence of any man upon the earth is the older daughter's reported claim. It is not adopted as the narrator's assertion of worldwide extinction. The account's description of the father's unawareness is preserved.
The kinship prohibition is a later legal comparison, not a legal speech attributed to the daughters or a claim that the Genesis narrator explicitly issues that command in this scene.

The supplied Deuteronomy 2:9 has the land name Seir while addressing the Moabites and sons of Lot. That reading is not silently changed to another edition's Ar; the retained link concerns descent from Lot, not reconstructed territorial boundaries.
Genesis names the ancestor Amman and the people Ammanites, while Deuteronomy uses Ammon. Both English forms are retained and linked by the stated Lot ancestry rather than normalized away.

The warning over Sarah's marriage does not add an unreported physical encounter. The king's innocence plea and God's acknowledgement of his pure heart remain attributed statements. The actual Greek-based Exodus adultery prohibition is20:13, not a silently substituted common numbering.
The later law is a comparison of the specifically named paternal/maternal sister relationship, not a claim that the Mosaic command is being spoken to Abraham in this scene.

Retain the thousand didrachms, honour of Sarah's face and instruction to speak truth. No eye-covering idiom, modern currency conversion or identical illness in Pharaoh's earlier household is imported. The closed-womb condition and its healing remain explicit.

Direct recollection of Isaac's eighth-day circumcision at Acts7:8 is distinguished from later legislative or personal ritual parallels in Leviticus, Luke and Philippians. These are concrete ritual-timing matches, not identical birth events.

The supplied narrative says playing with Isaac. Paul's later persecution language and slave/free allegory are labelled as interpretation rather than substituted into Genesis. The promise in Isaac is not used to erase the separately retained blessing of Ishmael.

Retain the child-also-on-the-shoulder wording, child crying and God hearing the child. No alternative age reconstruction, transfer of the crying to Hagar, medical blindness or prediction of archery is added. Hagar's Egyptian background is supplied by16:1;25:12 identifies her son without itself repeating Egyptian.

The recurring diplomatic names and oath/well pattern do not establish that rulers across Abraham's and Isaac's generations are one historical individual. The target's We found no water reading at26:32 remains intact. Gifts in21:27 are not silently turned into a sacrifice.

The supplied action is planted a field, not a substituted tamarisk tree or grove. Calling on the Lord is compared with other worship scenes; no unreported altar is inserted here. The Everlasting God comparison uses actual Greek Psalm89:2.
The supplied command says high land, not Moriah, and beloved son. Hebrews uses its own only-son wording; that description is not used to erase Ishmael from Genesis.

Hebrews supplies the later resurrection-confidence interpretation. The actual return notice names Abraham and does not separately name Isaac; no extra return-party detail or theory of Isaac's absence is imposed.
The wood/cross carrying link is labelled thematic only. John's actual text says cross and does not name Isaac or quote Genesis; no independent claim of literary dependence is made.

Offering and binding are distinguished from accomplished slaughter. Hebrews' receiving back is explicitly figurative. The ram is caught in a sabek plant in the supplied source, which remains unchanged.
The supplied place-name The Lord Has Seen and the saying In the mountain the Lord appeared are preserved. No new etymology or independent geographical identification is claimed.
The source says inherit the cities of adversaries, retained beside Genesis24:60. Later Christ/seed interpretation is attributed to Galatians rather than inserted into Genesis.

Uz, Buz and Kemuel are not merged with every other similarly named figure or region. The supplied forms Azau, Tabek, Tochos and Mocha remain untouched. Milcah's line and Reumah's concubine branch remain distinct.
The community says king from God, which is not replaced by a familiar prince or prophet wording.

Double cave, four hundred didrachms and approved by merchants are retained. No monetary conversion or substitution of shekels is made, and all that entered the city is not expanded into an unquoted gate description.
The full-payment parallel preserves David's different owner, site and purpose. It does not harmonize the transaction amounts or make the acquisitions one event.
The transactions are compared as public acquisitions before witnesses. Ruth's marriage/inheritance setting is not identified with Abraham's burial acquisition.

The servant remains unnamed. The under-thigh oath is compared with the actual Joseph/Israel oath at47:29-31, without assigning an unreported ritual meaning or identifying this servant with a separately named steward.

The original instructions and servant's report are compared as repeated speech. The release clause concerning the woman's willingness and the reported clause concerning the family's giving her are retained as differently formulated conditions. The report's curse wording is not silently removed.

The servant's requested criterion, the narrated watering actions and the report are distinguished. No unreported audible speech or further divinatory system is added to the supplied speaking-in-his-mind wording.

Rebekah is Bethuel's daughter and Milcah/Nahor's granddaughter in the supplied family account. The broader daughter-of-my-master's-brother expression in the servant's speech is retained rather than used to invent a different direct parentage. One initial rationale was corrected during the second pass to state this hierarchy precisely.

Retain the supplied plural golden earrings, each a drachma in weight, and the bracelets' ten gold pieces. No nose-ring, half-shekel conversion or alternative chronology is imported. The narrated taking out and reported putting on of the gifts remain distinct.
The supplied righteousness-and-truth thanksgiving and Laban's blessed-be-the-Lord invitation are retained. The invitation is not recast as an explicit blessing pronounced on the servant.
Well meetings, family reporting and Laban's welcome are narrative parallels. The two wells are not identified, and different women, household parties and occasions remain distinct.

The family's attribution of the outcome to the Lord is identified as their spoken interpretation; no additional divine oracle is invented. Family permission and Rebekah's own willingness are both recorded without importing an independent historical legal reconstruction.
The supplied brothers plural, about-ten-days request, possessions at59 and maidservants at61 are retained. A nurse is not silently inserted into24:59 from another edition.
The blessing names thousands of ten thousands and adversaries' cities. The corresponding Genesis22:17 comparison preserves cities rather than replacing it with another edition's gates wording.

The Well of the Vision is linked to the identical label at25:11. Isaac's meditation is not independently restated as prayer. Rebekah leaped down in the supplied reading; her veil is not made into an unstated universal rule.

The servant calls the approaching Isaac his master in context; no conclusion about Abraham already being dead is added. Isaac enters his mother's house in the supplied text; it is not silently changed to Sarah's tent.

Genesis calls Keturah another wife while Chronicles calls her a concubine. No identification with Hagar or resolution of marital status is imposed. Genesis25:3 retains Teman and the expanded Dedan list; the available Chronicles unit has only Saba and Daidan for this branch. All differing English name forms remain quoted as supplied.

Nebaioth/Nabaioth, Massam/Mabsan, Mishma/Masma, Iduma/Idouma, Massa/Masse, Teman/Thaiman, Jetur/Jettour, Naphish/Naphes and Kedemah/Kedma forms are retained, with relationships compared by their actual catalogue positions. No merger with other biblical people bearing similar names is made.
The supplied statement is lived opposite all his brothers. It is not silently replaced with another edition's death wording.

The supplied Genesis says greater and lesser in an oracle about two peoples; Romans quotes older and younger and develops divine-election interpretation. That later interpretation and its wording are distinguished from claims added to Genesis.

The actual supplied Hosea heel-related passage is12:4. It places tripping the brother in the womb; Genesis narrates the hand holding Esau's heel at birth. Their particular retrospective and narrative wording is preserved.
Jacob remains without pretence, dwelling in a house, rather than being silently changed to a familiar tent-dweller wording or described as morally faultless in all later conduct.

The sworn sale and narrator's despised-birthright verdict are distinguished from Esau's later grievance about being supplanted. Hebrews' profane-sale interpretation is retained without asserting that the text attributes sexual misconduct to Esau or adjudicating the later repentance clause, which is not selected here.

Repeated Abimelech, Ahuzzath and Phicol names/roles form narrative parallels across the Abraham and Isaac accounts. No claim of one historical individual spanning the generations is made. Isaac playing with Rebekah is not expanded into an unreported act.
The harvest remains barley a hundredfold, and the property list retains much farmland. No general financial guarantee is inferred or a different edition's household-workforce wording substituted.

The supplied well/place names Injustice, Enmity, Broad Space and Well of the Oath remain intact. Separate ancestral oath/well stories are compared without requiring that every well is one physical well.
Isaac's accusation of hatred and the delegation's claim of good treatment remain differing reported perspectives. Neither is silently made a comprehensive narrator's judgment.
The actual morning departure of Laban is32:1 in this source. There is no separate31:55 unit; no missing verse was inserted.
The supplied servants say We found no water. This is retained alongside the earlier successful water discovery and subsequent naming; it is not normalized to a positive report.

Retain Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hivite, and the statement that they contended with Isaac and Rebekah. The different wife names and parentage in Genesis36 are compared as a separate family record, not automatically harmonized or renamed.
